items.title: SQLite: invalid create table DDL when schemaGenerator.createForeignKeyConstraints is disabled
items.body:
### Describe the bug

With `schemaGenerator: { createForeignKeyConstraints: false }`, the SQLite driver generates invalid `create table` DDL for entities with relations. Every foreign key adds an empty item to the column list:

```sql
create table `book` (`id` integer not null primary key autoincrement, `author_id` integer not null, `editor_id` integer not null, , );
```

So `orm.schema.create()` / `refresh()` fails with `near ",": syntax error`.

Expected:

```sql
create table `book` (`id` integer not null primary key autoincrement, `author_id` integer not null, `editor_id` integer not null);
```


### Reproduction

https://github.com/jbl428/reproduction (`src/create-foreign-key-constraints.test.ts`)

Minimal setup: two `@ManyToOne` relations, in-memory SQLite, `createForeignKeyConstraints: false`. The `current behavior` tests assert the broken output and the `expected behavior` tests fail until the bug is fixed.


### What driver are you using?

@mikro-orm/sqlite

### MikroORM version

7.2.3

### Node.js version

v22.22.3, TypeScript 5.8

### Operating system

macOS 26.6.2

items.title: Declare sequence / identity start value and increment in entity metadata
items.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

There is no way to declare the start value (or increment) of an autoincrement / identity column in entity metadata. Today the only option is raw SQL in a migration (`alter sequence ... restart with 1000`, `alter table ... auto_increment = 1000`).

This has two practical problems:

- Anything built from metadata ignores it: `schema:create`, `schema:refresh`, `orm.schema.refreshDatabase()` in tests. Every test setup has to repeat the raw SQL after the schema is created.
- The value is invisible in the model, so it can drift between environments and nothing reports it.

This was asked in #7158. @B4nan's questions there were: how should it work, what about schema diffing, and should it be respected only when the sequence is created? The proposal below tries to answer them.

The closest thing that works today has a destructive side effect. On Postgres, `generated` is passed through into the DDL, so this creates the column correctly:

```ts
id: { type: 'number', primary: true, generated: 'identity (start with 1000)' }
// create table "thing" ("id" int generated always as identity (start with 1000) not null primary key, ...)
// first insert gets id 1000
```

But introspection reads the column back as plain `identity`, so the very next `getUpdateSchemaSQL()` on an unchanged schema wants to drop and re-add the primary key:

```sql
alter table "thing" drop column "id";
alter table "thing" add "id" int generated always as identity (start with 1000) not null primary key;
```

(Reproduced on 7.2.1 with `@mikro-orm/pglite`.) `generated: 'by default as identity (start with 1000)'` doesn't work either, because only the exact string `'by default as identity'` is special-cased, so it renders as `generated always as by default as identity (...)`.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

A `sequence` option on autoincrement properties (decorators and `defineEntity`):

```ts
@PrimaryKey({ sequence: { startWith: 1000, incrementBy: 1 } })
id!: number;

@Property({ autoincrement: true, sequence: { startWith: 10000 } })
ref!: number;
```

Semantics per driver:

| Driver | On create | Diff on change |
|---|---|---|
| PostgreSQL, identity (`generated: 'identity'` / `'by default as identity'`) | `generated ... as identity (start with 1000 increment by 1)` | Compare with `information_schema.columns.identity_start` / `identity_increment`, emit `alter table ... alter column ... set start with X set increment by Y` |
| PostgreSQL, `serial` (the default) | `alter sequence "thing_id_seq" start with 1000 increment by 1 restart` right after `create table` (the table is empty at that point) | Compare with `pg_sequences.start_value` / `increment_by`, emit `alter sequence ... start with X increment by Y` |
| MySQL / MariaDB | `create table ... auto_increment = 1000` | None. `information_schema.tables.AUTO_INCREMENT` is "the next AUTO_INCREMENT value", not a declared start, so it can't be diffed. Create-only. |
| SQLite (AUTOINCREMENT tables) | `insert into sqlite_sequence (name, seq) values ('thing', 999)` after create | None. Create-only. |
| MSSQL | `identity(1000, 1)` instead of the hardcoded `identity(1,1)` | None. SQL Server can't alter the identity property of an existing column (the schema helper already works around this). Create-only. |

Answers to the questions in #7158:

1. **Only on create?** Always on create. On Postgres the diff can also compare the declared values with the introspected ones. Per the Postgres docs, `ALTER SEQUENCE ... START WITH` "changes the recorded start value of the sequence. This has no effect on the current sequence value", so the diff never touches existing data. Moving the current value of an existing sequence (`restart`) stays an explicit data-level action in a migration.
2. **Schema diffing:** the start/increment become part of the column's sequence metadata and are compared like defaults or types. Drivers that can't read back a declared start (MySQL, SQLite, MSSQL) skip it in the diff, so there are no spurious migrations.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

- Raw SQL in a migration: works for migrated databases, but not for `schema:create` / `refreshDatabase()`, and the value isn't visible in the model.
- `generated: 'identity (start with N)'`: creates the right DDL, but every later diff drops and re-adds the PK column (see above).
- `default: raw("nextval('custom_seq')")` with a hand-made sequence: the ORM doesn't create or track the sequence, so it has to be created separately in every environment.

**Additional context**

Prior art:

- EF Core: `modelBuilder.HasSequence<int>("OrderNumbers").StartsAt(1000).IncrementsBy(5)`; SQL Server `UseIdentityColumn(seed, increment)`; Npgsql `HasIdentityOptions(startValue: 100)`
- JPA / Hibernate: `@SequenceGenerator(initialValue = 1000, allocationSize = ...)`
- Drizzle: `pgSequence('name', { startWith: 100, increment: 2 })`, `generatedAlwaysAsIdentity({ startWith: 100 })`

Paginated orderBy on a to-one relation uses the wrong alias when another populated relation has a same-named json property
items.body:
### Describe the bug

Ordering a paginated query by a to-one relation picks the wrong table alias as soon as another, **populated**, to-one relation has a property of the same name typed as `json`.

Filtering on a M:N relation makes the query return duplicate rows, so `limit` makes MikroORM select the ids in a grouped sub-query first. The `orderBy` term is wrapped in `MIN()` for that sub-query, and there the alias comes from the populated relation instead of the one named in `orderBy`. The two `ORDER BY` clauses of the same query end up naming different columns:

**The property must be `json` for this to happen.** With a plain string column on both relations the alias stays correct, which is what made this hard to narrow down.

### Two symptoms

On **SQLite** nothing fails: `MIN()` accepts the mismatched column, the sub-query keeps the wrong row, and the caller silently gets a different page than it asked for.

On **PostgreSQL** the query does not run at all, because the mismatched column is `jsonb`:

```
DriverException: function min(jsonb) does not exist
 - hint: No function matches the given name and argument types. You might need to add explicit type casts.
```

That is how we found it — a working GraphQL endpoint started returning a 500 after a routine patch update.

### Affected versions

| Version | Sub-query `ORDER BY` | SQLite | PostgreSQL |
|---|---|---|---|
| 7.1.5 | correct alias | ok | ok |
| 7.1.6 | wrong alias | wrong page, silent | `function min(jsonb) does not exist` |
| 7.2.1 | wrong alias | wrong page, silent | `function min(jsonb) does not exist` |

First bad version is **7.1.6**. The only change in that release touching this path is *"sql: support orderBy on persist(false) virtual fields with pagination"* (#7979).

### Reproduction

https://github.com/laurentmalgras/mikro-orm-reproduction/tree/orderby-alias-lost-in-pagination-subquery

`npm test` — `src/orderby-alias-pagination.test.ts` fails. In-memory SQLite, four entities, no external database needed.

`Task` has two to-one relations, `questionnaire` (json `name`) and `contributingEntity` (string `name`), plus a M:N `assignedContributors`:

```ts
await orm.em.find(
  Task,
  { assignedContributors: { id: { $in: [contributor.id] } } },
  {
    limit: 1,
    orderBy: { contributingEntity: { name: 'ASC' } },
    populate: ['questionnaire'],
  },
);
```

The emitted SQL, where `q1` is `questionnaire` and `c3` is `contributingEntity`:

```sql
-- sub-query
... group by `t0`.`id` order by min(`q1`.`name`) asc limit 1
-- outer query
... order by `c3`.`name` asc
```

The two fixtures are seeded so the orderings disagree: by `contributingEntity.name` taskA comes first, by `questionnaire.name` taskB does. The test asserts the cause and the consequence separately, so the failure names the defect directly:

```
AssertionError: expected 'q1' to be 'c3'
```

### What driver are you using?

@mikro-orm/postgresql

### MikroORM version

7.1.14 (first bad: 7.1.6, last good: 7.1.5)

### Node.js version

Node.js v24.11.0, TypeScript 5.9.3

### Operating system

_No response_

items.title: Joined populate throws when embedded property has the same name as its column
items.body:
### Describe the bug

After upgrading from v6 to v7, populating a relation with the joined strategy started throwing for one of our entities.

The entity has an embeddable with a single property, and that property's column has the same name as the embedded property itself (`User.password` -> `Password.value` stored in the `password` column, `prefix: ''`). Loading `User` directly works, `select-in` works, only the joined populate fails:

```
DriverException: Cannot use 'as u1__password' alias on embedded property 'u1.password' because it expands to multiple columns. Alias individual fields instead (e.g. 'u1.password.propertyName as u1__password').
```

The error message was confusing to me since the embeddable only has one column and I'm not aliasing anything myself, the alias comes from the populate. My guess is `u1.password` gets resolved to the embedded property instead of the `password` column.

v6 had a problem with the same setup too, just a different one: the joined load works, but if you then change another entity and flush, it tries to update `user` with nothing in it:

```
Empty .update() call detected! Update data does not contain any values to update. This will result in a faulty query. Table: `user`. Columns: .
```

Again only after a joined load, select-in is fine.

Renaming the embedded property (we went with `hashedPassword`) makes both go away, so we're fine for now, but it took a while to figure out what was going on.

Might be related to #8271 / #8272, but it still fails on 7.2.1 and on the current `next`, which should already have that fix.

### Reproduction

https://github.com/JH8459/reproduction

`src/example.test.ts` has 4 tests. direct load and select-in pass, joined populate and the flush one fail.

- 7.2.1-dev.24 (next): joined populate + flush fail
- 7.2.1, 7.2.0: same
- 6.6.16: joined populate passes, flush fails with the empty update

I also tried it on mariadb 11.4, same results.

### What driver are you using?

@mikro-orm/sqlite (also reproduced with @mikro-orm/mariadb)

### MikroORM version

7.2.1-dev.24

### Node.js version

v24.11.0

items.title: Invalid SQL: `returning` leaks into the update sub-query for entities with a generated column
items.body:
### Describe the bug

When an entity has a `generated` column and `em.nativeUpdate()` is called with a condition that
traverses a relation, the generated SQL is invalid on PostgreSQL: the `returning` clause is emitted
**inside the inner sub-select** as well as on the outer `update`.

### Reproduction

https://github.com/laurentmalgras/mikro-orm-reproduction/tree/syntax-error-native-update-generated-column

Uses the `mikro-orm/reproduction` template as is, with in-memory SQLite:

```bash
npm install
npm test
```

`src/example.test.ts` holds two tests on the same `Book` entity, which has a `generated` column and a
`ManyToOne` to `Category`:

1. **`nativeUpdate` with a condition on a direct FK** — passes. No join, so no sub-query, and the
   `returning` clause stays on the `update` itself.
2. **`nativeUpdate` with a condition traversing a relation** (`{ category: { name: 'bar' } }`) —
   fails with `near "returning": syntax error`. The join forces the update into a sub-query, and the
   `returning` clause is emitted inside the inner `select` as well.

The first test is the control: same entity, same generated column, only the shape of the condition
differs.

Not driver specific. I ran the same test on both drivers: SQLite & PostgreSQL

### What driver are you using?

@mikro-orm/postgresql

7.1.5

Upgrade guide says em.transactional defaults to REQUIRES_NEW, Transactions page says NESTED
items.body:
Two docs pages disagree with each other on the default propagation for `em.transactional`, and I think one of them is just wrong.

Transactions page (`transactions.md#transaction-propagation`):

> By default, MikroORM uses `NESTED` propagation for explicit transactions via `em.transactional`. When you call `em.transactional()` within another transaction, it automatically creates a savepoint (nested transaction) rather than joining the existing transaction.

Upgrade guide (`upgrading-v6-to-v7.md`, "Default propagation in `@Transactional` is `REQUIRED`"):

> The previous default was `REQUIRES_NEW`, which always started a new transaction. `REQUIRES_NEW` remains the default for the `em.transactional` method.

Before opening a PR I went and checked which one matches reality. `em.transactional()` calls `TransactionManager.handle()`, which does `options.propagation ??= TransactionPropagation.NESTED` (`packages/core/src/utils/TransactionManager.ts:23`) — that's the only code path, there's no branch where it falls back to `REQUIRES_NEW`. The JSDoc on `EntityManager.transactional()` says the same thing in plain English ("a new savepoint (nested transaction) will be created by default"), and `tests/features/transactions/transaction-propagation.sqlite.test.ts` has a test specifically checking that nesting produces a `SAVEPOINT`. So the Transactions page is right and the upgrade guide sentence is wrong.

I also checked whether the upgrade guide used to be correct and just went stale. It didn't, as far as I can tell — the `options.propagation ??=` line hasn't changed since it was introduced in #6802, and it was already `NESTED` there. The wrong sentence got added later, in the same commit that changed the *decorator's* default to `REQUIRED`, but that commit didn't touch `em.transactional`'s default at all (only a type signature widening). So it looks like the sentence was wrong from the moment it was written, probably a mix-up between "the decorator used to default to REQUIRES_NEW" and "em.transactional still defaults to REQUIRES_NEW."

Same sentence shows up in both `docs/docs/upgrading-v6-to-v7.md` and the `version-7.2` snapshot, word for word.

Proposed fix, matching how the Transactions page already phrases it:

> `NESTED` remains the default for the `em.transactional` method, which creates a savepoint when a transaction is already active.

Happy to send a PR for this — just didn't want to guess which of your own two pages was the intended source of truth before submitting the diff.

TPT: parent-table columns unreachable through a relation targeting a sub-class
items.body:
Hey @B4nan fast fix yesterday, thanks!! Another TPT bug below, similar to the last one there's a couple ways to go about it so filing an issue rather than PR.

Two defects when an `m:1` targets a **TPT sub-class**: a column on a parent table cannot be reached
through the relation. Verified on sqlite, PostgreSQL 16 and MSSQL 2025.

```ts
@Filter({ name: 'softDelete', cond: { deletedAt: null }, default: true })   // only needed for defect 2
@Entity({ inheritance: 'tpt' })
class Animal {
  @PrimaryKey() id!: number;
  @Property() name!: string;
  @Property({ nullable: true }) deletedAt?: Date;
}

@Entity()
class Dog extends Animal {
  @Property() breed!: string;
}

@Entity()
class Tag {
  @PrimaryKey() id!: number;
  @ManyToOne(() => Dog) dog!: Dog;   // must be non-nullable for defect 2
}
```

## Defect 1 — `where`/`orderBy` on an inherited property never joins the parent table

```ts
await em.find(Tag, { dog: { name: 'Rex' } }, { filters: false });
```
```sql
from `tag` as `t0` inner join `dog` as `d1` on `t0`.`dog_id` = `d1`.`id`
where `d1`.`name` = 'Rex'          -- `animal` is never joined
```
`no such column: d1.name` / `column d1.name does not exist` / `Invalid column name 'name'`.

Also affects `orderBy`, `count`, `$in`, `groupBy` and `qb.joinAndSelect()`. Adding
`populate: ['dog'], strategy: 'joined'` to the query above makes it pass — populating adds the join
the criteria path does not. In a 3-level hierarchy it is any column not on the leaf table, not just
the root's: `where { puppy: { breed } }` fails too.

**Cause.** `applyTPTJoins()` walks the parent chain of `this.mainAlias.meta` only.
`AbstractSqlDriver.addTPTParentJoinsForRelation()` does the right walk for a relation target, but is
only reachable from `getFieldsForJoinedLoad()`, i.e. the joined-populate path. The criteria auto-join
(`ObjectCriteriaNode` → `joinReference()`) never calls it.

## Defect 2 — a filter condition on an inherited column forward-references the parent join

Needs the relation to be **non-nullable** — nullable gives a `leftJoin`, which `processNestedJoins()`
nests for unrelated reasons, incidentally bringing the alias into scope.

```ts
await em.find(Tag, {});
```
```sql
from `tag` as `t0`
inner join `dog` as `d1` on `t0`.`dog_id` = `d1`.`id` and `a2`.`deleted_at` is null  -- a2 not in scope
inner join `animal` as `a2` on `d1`.`id` = `a2`.`id`
```
`missing FROM-clause entry for table "a2"` / `The multi-part identifier "a2.deleted_at" could not be
bound.` sqlite silently accepts it, which is presumably why the sqlite TPT suite does not catch it.

**Cause.** `mergeOnConditions()` attaches the condition to the join whose alias prefixes the key
(`d1.deletedAt`), but `getTPTAliasForProperty()` re-qualifies it to `a2` at render time.
`nestReferencedJoins()` guards against exactly this, but `condReferencesAlias()` is a literal
`startsWith`, so it never fires for an inherited column — and `mergeOnConditions()` does not call it
at all.

## Related, not addressed

- `#state.tptAlias` uses two keying schemes (bare `className` vs `leafAlias:className`); I could not
  make them collide, flagging as a latent trap only.
- Defect 2 is invisible on sqlite, so a regression test needs postgres/mssql or an SQL assertion.

I have a fix for both (~30 lines in `packages/sql`), green with no regressions — happy to PR. One
design fork if you want it: I nest the parent join into the sub-class join group, but attaching the
condition to the parent join's own `on` would be flatter. It also drops `protected` from
`addTPTParentJoinsForRelation()`, which you may want at a different seam.

## Reproduction

https://github.com/Subtletree/mikro-orm/tree/repro/tpt-relation-to-subtype

One commit on master (35092380a), one test file, no source changes.
`yarn test tpt-relation-to-subtype` → 6 failing, 3 passing. The 3 are controls (same relation reaching
a sub-class-owned property; reading the sub-class directly by an inherited property), so the failures
are attributable to going through the relation rather than to TPT generally.

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| MikroORM version | master @ `35092380a` (unreleased; 7.1.14 is the latest published and predates #8227 / #8228 / #8229) |
| Driver | `@mikro-orm/sqlite`, `@mikro-orm/postgresql`, `@mikro-orm/mssql` |
| Node.js | 22.20.0 |
| OS | Ubuntu 24.04 (WSL2) |

items.title: TPT: the version property is applied to every table in the hierarchy, not the one that declares it
items.body:
# Describe the bug Under `inheritance: 'tpt'`, the version column physically exists only on the table of the entity that **declares** it. But `meta.versionProperty` resolves on every metadata in the hierarchy, because children inherit the root's properties. The write path never distinguishes the two, so the version bump, the optimistic lock predicate and the returning clause are applied to tables that have no version column. With the version property on the root, updating a column owned by a child table emits: ```sql -- root table, correct update `animal` set `name` = ?, `version` = ? where `id` = ? and `version` = ? returning `version` -- child table, invalid: `dog` has no version column update `dog` set `breed` = ?, `version` = ? where `id` = ? and `version` = ? returning `version` ``` ``` InvalidFieldNameException: no such column: version ``` The batched path fails the same way: ```sql update `dog` set `breed` = case when (`id` = ?) then ? when (`id` = ?) then ? else `breed` end, `version` = `version` + 1 where `id` in (?, ?) returning `id`, `version` ``` Removing the version property from the hierarchy makes the same update succeed, so the version handling is the trigger. Any update touching a child-owned column hits this, including the ordinary case of changing a root field and a child field in the same flush. The version property need not be on the root, and when it is declared lower the same gap appears from the opposite direction — the code assumes *the root* holds the column rather than assuming *every* table does: - **batched update** → `Error: Trying to query by not existing property Bird.version`, because `ChangeSetPersister.checkOptimisticLocks` queries `meta.root`. - **single-row update of a column owned above the declaring table** → fails **silently**. Only ``update `bird` set `name` = ? where `id` = ?`` is emitted: no bump, no lock predicate, no error. The update escapes optimistic locking and a concurrent writer's change is lost. This is arguably the most serious of the set, since nothing surfaces. **Expected:** the bump and the version predicate should apply only to the table that declares the version column — not necessarily the root — and to no other table in the hierarchy. Optimistic locking should still be enforced there. ### A separate defect on the same code path TPT parent change sets are never assigned `originalEntity` (`UnitOfWork.createTPTChangeSets` sets it only on the leaf), so a **batched** update of a **root**-owned column throws before reaching any of the above: ``` TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'id') at Utils.getPrimaryKeyCond (packages/core/src/utils/Utils.ts:611) at ChangeSetPersister.checkOptimisticLocks (packages/core/src/unit-of-work/ChangeSetPersister.ts:495) ``` Not about versioning as such — `checkConcurrencyKeys` reads the same field, so `concurrencyCheck` on a TPT entity hits it too. Included here because it is on the same path and any fix has to deal with it, but it is an independent bug.
Where it comes from These read `meta.versionProperty` / `prop.version` without asking whether *this* table owns the column: | Location | Effect | |---|---| | `core` `ChangeSetPersister.updateEntity` | version predicate in the non-declaring table's WHERE | | `core` `ChangeSetPersister.checkOptimisticLocks` | duplicate lock check per table, and queries `meta.root` rather than the declaring table | | `core` `ChangeSetPersister.reloadVersionValues` | redundant version reload per table on drivers without `RETURNING` | | `sql` `QueryBuilderHelper.updateVersionProperty` | `version = version + 1` in the non-declaring table's SET | | `sql` `AbstractSqlDriver.nativeUpdate` | version in the returning list | | `sql` `AbstractSqlDriver.nativeUpdateMany` | version bump in the batched update | | `sql` `AbstractSqlDriver.nativeUpdateMany` | version in the batched returning list | For comparison the INSERT path already handles this, via the existing `getTableProps()` helper in `AbstractSqlDriver`; the UPDATE path never got the same treatment. A further wrinkle for whoever fixes it: when *only* columns outside the declaring table change, `createTPTChangeSets` skips that table (empty payload) and `getChangeSetGroups` drops empty-payload UPDATE change sets, so no statement is emitted for it at all. Scoping the version handling alone therefore stops the crash but leaves the version un-bumped and a stale version un-rejected — the silent case above. Keeping the declaring table's change set alive for versioned hierarchies addresses it.
The schema generator already decides where the column lives This is a DML/DDL disagreement rather than an open design question. `SchemaGenerator` places the version column on the table of the entity that declares it, verified by generating the schema: | version declared on | table carrying the column | |---|---| | root | root only | | a middle entity | that middle table only | Child tables never get one. The docs state the same principle for the adjacent case — *"Index expressions, check constraints, and generated column callbacks for a TPT entity only have access to columns in that entity's own table"* — and `transactions.md` describes optimistic locking as an entity-level guarantee. The write path honours neither.
Related, not addressed - `getOnConflictReturningFields` (`core/src/utils/upsert-utils.ts`) has the same unscoped read, so a TPT child upsert names `version` in its `returning`. Latent, because TPT upsert already fails earlier for an unrelated reason (root columns end up in the child insert). - `generated` columns have the identical defect in both `returning` lists — a TPT child names its parent's generated columns. - `concurrencyCheck` combined with TPT does not work either, before or after any of the above: the payload split means the child's change set never carries the root's concurrency key.
### Why this is an issue rather than a pull request I have a fix that is green — the reproduction below passes, the SQLite suite passes, and the MySQL/MariaDB non-`RETURNING` path is covered — but the right shape depends on a call that seems yours to make: **(a) Localized.** Add an `EntityMetadata.ownsVersionProperty()` predicate and gate every write-path reader in the table above on it. Contained, no public API change. But `meta.versionProperty` stays truthy-but-meaningless on TPT children, so every future reader has to remember to ask the second question — I missed three of those readers on my first pass, which is the argument against it. **(b) Fix the invariant.** Stop setting `versionProperty` on TPT child metadata so that it means "this table has the column" by construction, and give the lock and validation APIs (`em.lock`, `checkLockRequirements`, `MetadataValidator`, `OptimisticLockError`) an explicit hierarchy-wide lookup. Fewer places to remember, and it fails closed. The cost is that `versionProperty` is public, user-settable config — `defineEntity`'s `versionProperty?: AllKeys` accepts inherited keys — so its meaning would change for anyone reading or setting it. Happy to send either as a PR, or to leave it with you. # Reproduction Branch with the failing test, cut from `master` at bc1063e31, containing nothing but the test file: https://github.com/Subtletree/mikro-orm/tree/repro/tpt-version-property ```sh yarn vitest run tests/features/table-per-type-inheritance/tpt-version-property.test.ts ``` Runs on SQLite (`:memory:`) with no external database and no containers. On `master` (bc1063e31): **2 pass, 5 fail**. The two passing tests are deliberate controls — a root-owned column update, and a child-owned column update on an identical hierarchy with no version property — so the failures are attributable to the version handling rather than to TPT generally. The faulty code is in `@mikro-orm/core` and `@mikro-orm/sql`, shared by every SQL driver, so it is not dialect-specific. I first hit this on MSSQL (`Invalid column name 'RowVersion'`) and separately confirmed the same failure on PostgreSQL (`column "version" does not exist`) with an equivalent entity setup; the linked test is SQLite-only so that it runs anywhere. # What driver are you using? @mikro-orm/sqlite (also observed on @mikro-orm/postgresql and @mikro-orm/mssql) # MikroORM version 7.1.14 (also reproduced on 7.1.11) # Node.js version v22.20.0, TypeScript 7.0.2 # Operating system Linux (WSL2)

items.body:
### Describe the bug

`QueryBuilder.applyJoinedFilters()` iterates `this.#state.autoJoinedPaths` with `for…of`, while `CriteriaNode.process()` — called inside that loop — pushes new paths onto the same array via `qb.scheduleFilterCheck()`. Array iterators are live, so the loop visits what it just appended.

When two entity filters reference each other through relations, this never terminates. Each lap schedules the next lap's joins and the criteria-node graph doubles, until the process dies with `JavaScript heap out of memory`. No error, no cycle detection, no depth cap.

Works in v6.6.14, fails in v7.1.14.

### Reproduction

https://github.com/jonasnilsberg/mikro-orm-filter-cycle-repro

```
npm install && node --max-old-space-size=256 repro.mjs   # 7.1.14 -> OOM
cd v6-control && npm install && node repro.mjs           # 6.6.14 -> ok
```

The heap cap only makes it fail fast; it OOMs at any size.

Three entities, two filters that traverse relations and close a cycle
(`ManagementObject → deviations → DeviationType → deviations → managementObject → …`):

```js
// ManagementObject
auth: { cond: ({ company }) => ({
  $or: [{ company }, { deviations: { type: { identifier: company } } }] }), default: true }

// DeviationType
auth: { cond: ({ company }) => ({ deviations: { managementObject: { company } } }), default: true }
```

```js
await em.find(ManagementObject, { deviations: { type: { identifier: "x" } } });
```

Both filters must traverse relations — one relational plus one scalar terminates fine.

### Actual

Instrumenting the loop shows `autoJoinedPaths` growing in lockstep with the iteration index:

```
iter=5  len=8   DeviationType.deviations
iter=6  len=8   DeviationType.deviations.managementObject
iter=7  len=10  DeviationType.deviations          <- cycle
iter=75 len=78  ...
FATAL ERROR: heap out of memory
```

A heap snapshot at the limit holds 131,073 (2^17 + 1) `ObjectCriteriaNode` instances, consistent with doubling once per cycle.

### Expected

The query completes, or MikroORM throws a descriptive error about the cyclic filter graph.

### Root cause

v6 stripped nested conditions from a relation-level filter and skipped the join when nothing scalar remained:

```js
if (!Utils.hasObjectKeys(cond)) continue;
```

A purely-nested filter was therefore discarded, so no cycle could form. v7 dropped that early exit and moved a `process()` call in front of the stripping:

```js
const criteriaNode = CriteriaNodeFactory.createNode(this.metadata, join.prop.targetMeta.class, cond);
cond = criteriaNode.process(this, { matchPopulateJoins: true, filter: true, … });
```

Resolving nested filter conditions into real joins looks like a deliberate improvement over v6 silently dropping them — the problem is only that the new traversal has no termination condition.

That same removed early exit also causes #8210, where a nested filter path binds to a join alias from a sibling branch. Two failure modes, one origin: cyclic filter graphs run away here, duplicated relations misresolve there.

### Versions

| Dependency | Version |
| ---------- | ------- |
| node | 22.23.1 |
| mikro-orm | 7.1.14 (fails; also 7.1.11, 7.1.12) / 6.6.14 (works) |
| your-driver | `@mikro-orm/sqlite` (code path is in `@mikro-orm/sql`, so all SQL drivers) |

items.title: Relation filter binds to a sibling branch's join alias, producing a forward alias reference
items.body:
### Describe the bug

When two default filters on an entity each traverse the same to-many relation, it gets auto-joined twice, in two branches. A filter on the *target* entity is merged into the `on` clause of both joins — but a nested relation path inside that filter resolves to a join created under the *other* branch. That alias renders later, so the query is rejected:

```
sqlite:   ON clause references tables to its right
postgres: missing FROM-clause entry for table "u3"
```

Works in v6.6.16, fails in v7.1.14.

### Reproduction

https://github.com/jonasnilsberg/mikro-orm-v7-sibling-branch-alias

```
npm install && node repro.mjs                    # 7.1.14 -> throws
cd v6-control && npm install && node repro.mjs   # 6.6.16 -> ok
```

`Mobile 1--* ManagementObject *--1 User *--1 Location`. Two filters on `Mobile` — one scalar-only (`managementObjects.status`), one traversing `managementObjects.user.location` — plus a `{ user: { location: 1 } }` filter on `ManagementObject`. Then `em.find(Mobile, {})`.

### Actual

```sql
select m0.* from mobile m0
left join management_object m1
  on m0.id = m1.mobile_id and u3.location_id = ?          -- u3 not in scope yet
left join (management_object m2 left join user u3 on m2.user_id = u3.id)
  on m0.id = m2.mobile_id and u3.location_id = ?
where m1.status in (?, ?) and u3.location_id = ?
```

`u3` belongs to m2's branch, so m1's `on` clause is both invalid SQL and pointing at the wrong row.

### Expected

m1 resolves `user` to its own join:

```sql
left join (management_object m1 left join user u4 on m1.user_id = u4.id)
  on m0.id = m1.mobile_id and u4.location_id = ?
```

### Root cause

`applyJoinedFilters()` processes the filter with `ignoreBranching: true`, so `getJoinForPath()` strips `[\d+]` and matches across branches:

```
want = Mobile[0].managementObjects.user  ->  u3 @ Mobile[1].managementObjects.user
```

`nestReferencedJoins()` (added for #7681, #8090, #8099) would normally fold a referenced join into the `on` clause, but it only scans the join's own subtree — and `u3`'s owner is `m2`. Folding wouldn't be right here anyway; m1 needs its own join.

The same removed early exit in `applyJoinedFilters()` also causes #8211, where a cyclic filter graph expands until the process runs out of memory. Two failure modes, one origin.

Skipping candidates whose branch markers conflict, in the two branch-insensitive lookups in `getJoinForPath()`, produces the expected SQL. Happy to open a PR if that's the direction you'd take.

### Versions

| Dependency | Version |
| ---------- | ------- |
| node | 22.23.1 |
| mikro-orm | 7.1.14 (fails) / 6.6.16 (works) |
| your-driver | `@mikro-orm/sqlite` |

items.title: Key decorator metadata registry by class reference (_id), not class name — minified builds with mangled class names corrupt discovery
items.body:
# Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

Production bundlers that mangle class names still corrupt MikroORM v7's decorator metadata registry. This has become acute with Next.js 16, where Turbopack is the default production bundler, its minifier mangles server-side class names, and there is currently no `keep_classnames` escape hatch (tracked upstream in vercel/next.js#96574, where the Turbopack team's position is that depending on constructor names is a library-level issue).

Minimal reproduction (self-contained, in-memory SQLite, four decorator entities): https://github.com/andres-dejesus/turbopack-mikroorm-mangling-repro

With default Turbopack minification, discovery fails during build-time prerendering:

```
Error [MetadataError]: Duplicate table names are not allowed: reactions
```

In our 24-entity production app the same root cause surfaces at decorator-registration time instead:

```
Error [MetadataError]: Multiple property decorators used on 'd.user' property
```

(the entity class minified to `d`, colliding with another class also minified to `d`).

This is with every known mitigation already applied: explicit `type` on every property (per discussion #6868 — no reliance on `emitDecoratorMetadata` reflection), explicit `tableName` on every entity, and explicit entity arrays (no folder-based discovery).

# Describe the solution you'd like

v7 already went partway here: `MetadataStorage` carries a per-class `_id` and an id-keyed map, and relations resolve through class references. But the registry still maintains `className`-keyed maps alongside, and the decorator registration path collides when two mangled classes share a short name.

The ask: key the decorator metadata registry off the existing `_id`/class-reference machinery end to end, so that mangled class names degrade only error-message readability, never correctness. (STI and other genuinely name-dependent features could keep requiring stable names, documented as such.)

# Describe alternatives you've considered

- `EntitySchema` with explicit `name` — works, but means abandoning the decorator API across the app.
- Bundler-side `keep_classnames` — requested on the Next.js side in vercel/next.js#96574; a team member has signaled openness, but a library-side fix would make MikroORM robust on every bundler with no config, and the two fixes are complementary.
- Disabling server minification — works today on webpack (`experimental.serverMinification: false`), silently ignored by Turbopack; the only Turbopack workaround is disabling minification globally, including client bundles.

# Additional context

MikroORM 7.1.9, `@mikro-orm/decorators` legacy decorators, Next.js 16.3.0. The reproduction repo includes the full pass/fail matrix (Turbopack minified fails; Turbopack unminified and webpack with `serverMinification: false` both pass). Happy to test any canary against it and against our production app.

items.body:
### Describe the bug

`schemaGenerator.skipTables` is honored by `migration:create` but not when `Migrator.runMigrations()` rewrites the migration snapshot from live introspection after `migration:up` / `migration:down`. A table present in the DB but excluded via `skipTables` (e.g. an externally-owned/connector table) leaks into the snapshot after `up()`. The next `migration:create` then diffs the poisoned snapshot against entity metadata and emits a spurious `DROP TABLE` for the skipped table.

### Reproduction

Minimal, self-contained SQLite repro (no external DB): [repro.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30457472/repro.txt)

`npm install && node repro.mjs # exit 1 = bug`

Output on stock 7.1.4:
```
after createInitial(): snapshot contains "foreign_table"? -> false
after up():                     snapshot contains "foreign_table"? -> true
next createMigration() emits DROP TABLE "foreign_table"? -> true
```

### Expected behavior

A table listed in `skipTables` should never appear in the snapshot, regardless of whether it was written by `migration:create` (metadata/target) or by `migration:up`/`down` (introspection). No `DROP TABLE` should be generated for it.

### Root cause / suggested fix

packages/migrations/src/Migrator.ts → runMigrations():
```
const schema = await DatabaseSchema.create(
  this.em.getConnection(), this.em.getPlatform(), this.config,
  undefined, undefined, undefined,
  /* skipTables */ undefined, /* skipViews */ undefined, ctx);
```
`skipTables`/`skipViews` are passed as `undefined`, whereas `SqlSchemaGenerator` passes `this.options.skipTables`/`skipViews` in its own `DatabaseSchema.create` calls. Passing the `schemaGenerator` options through here fixes it (verified against the repro - exit 0).

### What driver are you using?

None

### MikroORM version

7.1.4 (also 7.1.7, 7.2.0-dev.0)

### Node.js version

v24.3.0

_No response_

Execute queries with bind parameters instead of inlining values into the SQL (v7 follow-up to #6829, with benchmarks)
items.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

In v7, `AbstractSqlConnection.execute()` still interpolates all parameters into the SQL text and executes with an empty bind array, even though the kysely foundation carries parameters natively:

```ts
// packages/sql/src/AbstractSqlConnection.ts (7.1.5 dist lines 195–222)
const formatted = this.platform.formatQuery(query, params);
// ...
const compiled = CompiledQuery.raw(q.formatted);   // parameters: []
```

Every executed statement therefore has a unique text (different literal values), which defeats everything keyed on statement identity downstream:

- server-side prepared statements / plan reuse on PostgreSQL (and driver-side statement caches — this is where I ran into it, benchmarking MikroORM over a `pg.Pool`-compatible driver with a statement cache: it can never engage, because no query text ever repeats),
- `pg_stat_statements`-style observability (every execution is a distinct entry pre-normalization),
- any proxy/pooler feature keyed on parameterized statements.

I'm aware of #6829, where this was discussed for the knex era and described as deliberate (sqlite's low parameter limit, "performance reasons"), with the note that v7 would be the place to experiment and that the fix wouldn't be tricky there. This is that experiment, with numbers.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Compile the existing `?` placeholders to the dialect's bind placeholders and pass `q.params` through — `CompiledQuery.raw(sql, parameters)` already accepts them. I patched the 7.1.5 dist with a compile step that mirrors `Platform.formatQuery`'s walk exactly (`??` identifiers stay inlined — they can't be bound; `\?` stays a literal `?`; adjacent-`?` semantics preserved) but emits `$1..$n` and collects values:

```ts
compileParameterized(sql, params) {
  if (params.length === 0) return CompiledQuery.raw(sql);
  // formatQuery's exact walk, emitting `$${++n}` + values.push(...) for `?`,
  // this.platform.quoteIdentifier(...) for `??`, literal `?` for `\?`
  return CompiledQuery.raw(ret, values);
}
```

Measured on the ORM benchmark harness of [prisma-pglite-bridge](https://github.com/drudolf/prisma-pglite-bridge) (5 ops × 300 iterations × 3 repeats, spread-checked medians), MikroORM 7.1.5, two drivers:

Over a `pg.Pool`-compatible driver (kysely `PostgresDialect` via `driverOptions`), p50:

| op | inlined | parameterized | delta |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| single insert | 0.28ms | 0.24ms | −14% |
| select where | 0.45ms | 0.38ms | −16% |
| tx (r+w) | 1.12ms | 0.90ms | −20% |
| findMany | 1.58ms | 1.52ms | −4% |
| join | 3.58ms | 3.40ms | −5% |

p99 improves more (−25% insert, −33% where, −30% tx). And notably, the official `@mikro-orm/pglite` driver **also** gets faster with the same patch (insert 0.50→0.41ms p50, tx 1.94→1.50ms) — the win isn't specific to one driver, and on a real PostgreSQL server, bind parameters additionally unlock server-side plan reuse that an embedded benchmark can't show.

The concerns from #6829, addressed:

- *Parameter-count limits*: real — PostgreSQL caps binds at 65535, sqlite defaults far lower. A guard that falls back to the current formatted execution when `params.length` exceeds a per-dialect threshold keeps huge batch inserts working exactly as today, while the overwhelmingly common small-arity queries get parameterized.
- *Type fidelity*: values reach the driver as JS values instead of pre-rendered literals, so the serialization decisions `quoteValue` makes today (e.g. JSON-tagged embeddables → stringify) need to move into a value-mapping pass for the bind array. Drivers handle `Date`/`Buffer` natively.
- *Logging*: `getSql`/`logQuery` can keep using `q.formatted` — human-readable logs, parameterized execution. (This would also give #6499 a natural path.)
- `stream()` inlines the same way and would want the same treatment.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

- Leaving it as is: every consumer keyed on statement identity stays permanently cold; observability tooling sees unique texts forever.
- Driver-side auto-parameterization (extracting literals back out of the formatted SQL): unsound in general — this really belongs where the parameters still exist.
- Dialect-gating: enabling bind-parameter execution for postgres only (where the win is largest and the limit is highest) would sidestep the sqlite parameter-limit concern entirely, at the cost of divergent execution paths.

**Additional context**

MikroORM 7.1.5, Node 24, benchmarked on macOS (arm64) against PGlite-backed drivers; correctness verified by the harness's value/transaction checks before timing, and by inspecting `pg_prepared_statements` (statement cache engages, K=2 promotion, with the patch; provably never engages without it). Happy to share the full dist patch and the benchmark setup.

items.title: TPT: base enum CHECK constraint duplicated onto child subtype tables
items.body:
### Describe the bug

For TPT entities with an enum on the base table, the generated schema duplicates the enum's CHECK constraint onto the child tables.

Below is a verbose AI description:

---

  With `inheritance: 'tpt'`, schema generation emits a **base** entity's enum `CHECK` constraint onto the **child** subtype table as well. In TPT the column lives only on the parent table, so the child-table CHECK references a non-existent column and the generated DDL is invalid — `schema.create()` / `migration:up` fails.

  - **sqlite:** `no such column: status`
  - **mssql:** error **207**, `Invalid column name 'status'`

  This is **driver-independent** — the wrong-table constraint is produced in the shared schema layer (`DatabaseSchema.fromMetadata`), so it reproduces on sqlite, mssql, postgres and mysql. The reproduction uses in-memory sqlite per the template guidance.

  ## Entities (defineEntity; same happens with the decorator API)

  ```ts
  enum Status { ACTIVE = 'active', INACTIVE = 'inactive' }

  const PersonSchema = defineEntity({
    name: 'Person', abstract: true, inheritance: 'tpt',
    properties: { id: p.integer().primary(), name: p.string(), status: p.enum(() => Status) },
  });
  class Person extends PersonSchema.class {}
  PersonSchema.setClass(Person);

  const EmployeeSchema = defineEntity({
    name: 'Employee', extends: PersonSchema,
    properties: { department: p.string() }, // no `status` here
  });
  class Employee extends EmployeeSchema.class {}
  EmployeeSchema.setClass(Employee);
  ```

  ## Expected

  The `status` CHECK is emitted on the `person` table only.

  ## Actual

  `getCreateSchemaSQL()` also emits a CHECK on `employee`, whose table has no `status` column:

  ```sql
  create table `person` (`id` integer not null primary key autoincrement, `name` text not null, `status` text check (`status` in ('active', 'inactive')) not null);
  create table `employee` (`department` text not null, `id` integer not null primary key, constraint `employee_id_foreign` foreign key (`id`) references `person` (`id`) on update cascade on delete cascade,
  constraint `employee_status_check` check (`status` in ('active', 'inactive')));
  -- the `employee` table has no `status` column
  ```

  `await orm.schema.create()` then throws `no such column: status`.

  ## Notes

 - The runtime persistence layer already handles this correctly — inserting an `Employee` writes `status` to `person` and only `department`/PK to `employee`.
  - It's only DDL generation that's wrong: `DatabaseSchema.fromMetadata` already restricts TPT child **columns** to `ownProps`, but the **checks** loop iterates `meta.checks` (including inherited entries) without that filter, so inherited enum CHECKs leak onto child tables.

### Reproduction

https://github.com/Subtletree/mikro-orm-tpt-check-repro

### What driver are you using?

@mikro-orm/mssql

### MikroORM version

7.1.4 also tested on 7.1.5-dev.26

### Node.js version

22.20.0

Ubuntu

items.title: TPT incompatible with polymorphic associations
items.body:
### Describe the bug

Polymorphic relations assume flat entities (one entity = one table). TPT breaks this because the discriminator resolution doesn't walk the inheritance hierarchy, and the JOIN generation doesn't account for the parent+child table split.

This is manifested in three issues:

1. INSERT: discriminator is null: When assigning a TPT child (e.g. Dog) to a polymorphic ref that lists the abstract parent (Animal), MikroORM resolves the discriminator from the concrete class. Since Dog isn't in the poly union, subject_type is written as null and the reference is silently corrupted.
2. SELECT: child table not joined: When populating the polymorphic relation, only the parent animal table is LEFT JOINed. The child dog table is never joined, so the entity hydrates as a bare Animal missing TPT child properties (e.g. breed).
3. TypeScript: ref(dog) not assignable: Dog extends Animal and Animal is in the union, but Reference<Dog> doesn't satisfy the polymorphic property type. Users must cast to work around it.

### Reproduction

items.body: ### Describe the bug Certain whitespace (I'm not sure what exactly) in the `expression` of view entities will cause migrations to never be complete.
